definition: The entryway or entrance hall of a Japanese home; the area where shoes are removed before stepping up into the house
meaningKo: 현관; 일본 가정의 신발을 벗는 입구 공간
etymology: 玄(げん, dark/deep) + 関(かん, gateway) → literally 'deep gateway'; originally a Zen Buddhist term referring to the profound entrance to enlightenment

rootBreakdown.root: 玄(げん, 깊은·현묘한) + 関(かん, 관문)

relatedWords: 玄関口 (げんかんぐち, entrance)
玄関先 (げんかんさき, doorstep)
contextSentence: ここは、玄関を置きます。

definition: Traditional; relating to customs, beliefs, and practices passed down through generations
meaningKo: 전통적인; 대대로 전해 내려온 관습이나 방식에 관한
etymology: 伝(でん, transmit) + 統(とう, lineage/unify) + 的(てき, -ic suffix) → 'of transmitted lineage'

rootBreakdown.root: 伝統(でんとう, 전통) + 的(てき, ~적인)

relatedWords: 伝統 (でんとう, tradition)
伝統工芸 (でんとうこうげい, traditional crafts)
contextSentence: 今日は私たちの伝統的な日本の家をお見せします。

definition: A Buddhist household altar; a cabinet containing a miniature shrine used for ancestor worship in Japanese homes
meaningKo: 불단; 일본 가정에서 조상을 모시는 불교식 제단
etymology: 仏(ぶつ, Buddha/Buddhist) + 壇(だん, altar platform) → 'Buddhist altar'

rootBreakdown.root: 仏(ぶつ, 불교·부처) + 壇(だん, 단상·제단)

relatedWords: 仏教 (ぶっきょう, Buddhism)
神棚 (かみだな, Shinto shelf)

definition: A traditional Japanese sliding door or window made of translucent paper stretched over a wooden lattice frame
meaningKo: 장지; 나무 격자 위에 반투명 한지를 붙인 전통 일본식 미닫이문
etymology: 障(しょう, obstruct/screen) + 子(じ, diminutive suffix for objects) → 'screening panel'

rootBreakdown.root: 障(しょう, 가리다·막다) + 子(じ, 물건을 나타내는 접미사)

relatedWords: ふすま (fusuma, opaque sliding door)
格子 (こうし, lattice)
contextSentence: 障子と言うことができます。

definition: A type of opaque sliding door used in traditional Japanese architecture to partition rooms; made of thick paper or fabric on a wooden frame
meaningKo: 후스마(미닫이문); 전통 일본 건축에서 방을 나누는 데 사용하는 불투명 미닫이문
etymology: 衾障子 (ふすましょうじ) → shortened to ふすま; 衾 means 'bedding/cover', originally referring to a screen that covered sleeping quarters

rootBreakdown.root: 衾(ふすま, 이불·덮개) + 障子(しょうじ, 미닫이문) → 줄여서 ふすま

relatedWords: 障子 (しょうじ, translucent sliding door)
引き戸 (ひきど, sliding door general)
contextSentence: この部屋はふすまで仕切ることができます。

definition: Pine, bamboo, and plum; a traditional Japanese grouping of three auspicious plants symbolizing good fortune, resilience, and perseverance
meaningKo: 송죽매(松竹梅); 소나무·대나무·매화나무를 뜻하는 일본의 전통적인 길상 식물 세 가지
etymology: 松(しょう, pine) + 竹(ちく, bamboo) + 梅(ばい, plum); a grouping derived from Chinese literary and visual arts tradition (歳寒三友)

rootBreakdown.root: 松(まつ/しょう, 소나무) + 竹(たけ/ちく, 대나무) + 梅(うめ/ばい, 매화)

relatedWords: 縁起物 (えんぎもの, good luck charm)
吉祥文様 (きっしょうもんよう, auspicious pattern)
contextSentence: 松竹梅と呼ばれています。

definition: Omen, luck; a sign or symbol believed to bring good fortune or bad luck
meaningKo: 길흉의 징조; 행운이나 불운을 가져온다고 여겨지는 징조나 상징
etymology: 縁(えん, fate/connection) + 起(き, arise/origin) → 'arising from karmic connection'; originally a Buddhist term

rootBreakdown.root: 縁(えん, 인연·연) + 起(き, 일어나다·기원)

relatedWords: 縁起が良い (えんぎがよい, good omen)
縁起担ぎ (えんぎかつぎ, superstition)
contextSentence: 日本の三つの縁起の良い木の中で

definition: To partition, divide, or separate a space using a partition or divider
etymology: 仕(し, do/serve) + 切る(きる, cut/divide) → 'to cut off/divide'
relatedWords: 仕切り (しきり, partition/divider)
区切る (くぎる, to divide/mark off)
contextSentence: この部屋はふすまで仕切ることができます。

definition: A gap, crack, or space between objects; in architecture, refers to deliberate spacing in lattice windows or screens
meaningKo: 틈, 간격; 물체 사이의 공간; 건축에서는 격자창 등의 의도적인 간격
etymology: 隙(すき, gap) + 間(ま/かん, interval/space) → 'space-interval'

rootBreakdown.root: 隙(すき, 틈·간격) + 間(ま, 사이·간격)

relatedWords: 隙間風 (すきまかぜ, draft through a gap)
格子 (こうし, lattice)
contextSentence: 隙間のある窓、格子窓があります。

definition: A lattice window; a traditional Japanese window design featuring a grid or crossed-bar pattern
meaningKo: 격자창; 나무 격자 무늬가 있는 전통 일본식 창문
etymology: 格子(こうし, lattice/grid) + 窓(まど, window) → 'lattice window'

rootBreakdown.root: 格子(こうし, 격자·바둑판 무늬) + 窓(まど, 창문)

relatedWords: 障子 (しょうじ, shoji screen)
窓枠 (まどわく, window frame)
contextSentence: 隙間のある窓、格子窓があります。

definition: To show (something to someone); the humble/polite form of 見せる (to show), used when the speaker does something for the listener
meaningKo: 보여 드리다; '보여주다'의 겸양어로, 청자를 위해 행동할 때 사용
etymology: お (honorific prefix) + 見せる (みせる, to show) + する (to do) → honorific construction
relatedWords: 見せる (みせる, to show)
お見せします (おみせします, I will show you, polite)
contextSentence: 今日は私たちの伝統的な日本の家をお見せします。

definition: Please tell me / please let me hear; a polite phrase requesting someone to share information or their thoughts
meaningKo: 이야기해 주세요; 의견이나 이야기를 들려달라는 정중한 표현
etymology: お (honorific prefix) + 聞かせ (きかせ, causative stem of 聞く, 'let hear') + ください (please do) → 'please let (me) hear'

rootBreakdown.root: 聞かせ(きかせ, 들려주다의 어간)

relatedWords: 聞く (きく, to hear/listen)
教えてください (おしえてください, please tell me)
contextSentence: 皆さんに質問があります。

definition: Akihabara; a district in Tokyo famous for electronics, anime, manga, and otaku culture
meaningKo: 아키하바라; 도쿄의 전자제품, 애니메이션, 만화, 오타쿠 문화로 유명한 지역
etymology: 秋(あき, autumn) + 葉(は, leaf) + 原(はら, field/plain) → 'autumn leaf field'; historical place name

rootBreakdown.root: 秋(あき, 가을) + 葉(は, 잎) + 原(はら, 벌판)

relatedWords: オタク (otaku, enthusiast/nerd)
アキバ (akiba, informal abbreviation for Akihabara)
contextSentence: 今、秋葉原の東京に住んでいます。

definition: Cute, adorable, charming; a highly versatile Japanese word expressing affection or aesthetic appeal
meaningKo: 귀여운, 사랑스러운; 애정이나 심미적 매력을 표현하는 일본어의 핵심 단어
etymology: 顔映し (かおはゆし) → old form かはゆし → contracted to かわいい; originally meant 'pitiful/embarrassing to look at' → shifted to mean 'lovable'

rootBreakdown.root: 顔映し (かおはゆし, 얼굴이 붉어지다·부끄럽다) 변형

relatedWords: かわいさ (かわいさ, cuteness)
可愛がる (かわいがる, to dote on)
contextSentence: この場所は本当にかわいいです。

definition: To be interested in (something); a common expression for expressing interest
etymology: 興味(きょうみ, interest) + が (subject marker) + ある (to exist/have) → 'interest exists'

rootBreakdown.root: 興味(きょうみ, 흥미·관심) + がある(존재하다)

relatedWords: 興味深い (きょうみぶかい, very interesting)
関心がある (かんしんがある, to have concern/interest)
contextSentence: 私は、日本の人に興味があります。
